findings.claim: The ordinary code-repair row guards on `lastVerdict !== "finding"`, an inversion that makes the repair path unreachable for exactly the states it exists to serve (a code finding).
findings.expected: Stage `review` selects row `open` and presents the ordered plan DISPATCH{role: reviewer} -> WRITE{artifact: reviewLog, format: reviewResult} -> NEXT. The artifact asserts this itself: fixtures/scenarios.json scenario `review-open` carries this exact state with expect.row = "open" and expect.effects = [DISPATCH, WRITE, NEXT], and body.md "## stage: review" states the judgment "Repair code findings; leave card-contract findings to planning."
findings.actual: `open` evaluates false ("finding" !== "finding" is false). No sibling row rescues the state: `broken-record` (line 39) additionally requires ordinal >= 3; `replan` (line 40) requires lastTarget === "card-contract"; `undecided`/`continue`/`unreviewed` (lines 41-43) require a lastVerdict of "unverified"/"pass"/"NONE". With zero matching rows the state falls to the synthetic unmatched row `BLOCK:review-unclassified` (the id documented by the artifact's own `unclassified` scenario), so a code finding halts with BLOCK instead of being repaired. The same dead end swallows the disposition-release path: {finding, code, ordinal 3, disposition "present"} fails `broken-record` on `disposition === "NONE"` and fails `open` on the inversion, so an explicitly dispositioned finding past the cycle bound BLOCKs instead of resuming repair.

Under first-match ordering `open` wins and the stage dispatches a reviewer and appends a reviewResult line for a verdict that is by definition unresolved, advancing past unverified evidence; under any other resolution rule the table is simply ambiguous, since `exclusive: false` declares no arbitration. The identical collision hits {lastVerdict "pass", lastTarget "code", reviewLogPresent "no"}, where `open` re-dispatches a reviewer although `continue` prescribes only WRITE -> NEXT. Dynamic confirmation is impossible in the shipped tree because the L0 import failure prevents the spec from loading, and no scenario in fixtures/scenarios.json pairs lastTarget "code" with a non-finding verdict.

answers.answer: Stage `signal` (spec.mjs:25). Its `done` is `s.signal.pass === "yes"` and signal.pass is "no", so signal is the active stage and nothing advances to `review`. Guard `read-only-session` (line 22) does not fire because session.readOnly is "no", so no effect is restricted. Ordered effect plan, exactly as declared: (1) RUN{check: "completion"} — execute the completion check; (2) WRITE{artifact: "signalRecord"} — append to state/signal.log (ARTIFACTS.signalRecord, writer review-flow, update "append", no template), matching the stage's `record: {kind: "file", artifact: "signalRecord"}`; (3) NEXT — hand off to stage `review`. This agrees with the artifact's own fixture `signal-open`, which expects stage "signal" with effects [RUN, WRITE, NEXT].

Intended: row `open` of TABLES.review, with the ordered plan DISPATCH{role: "reviewer"} -> WRITE{artifact: "reviewLog", format: "reviewResult"} -> NEXT. That is what fixtures/scenarios.json `review-open` asserts for this exact state and what body.md "## stage: review" ("Repair code findings") describes. As shipped, NO row applies. `open` (line 38) is guarded on `review.lastVerdict !== "finding"` and this verdict IS "finding", so it is false; `broken-record` needs ordinal >= 3 (here 1); `replan` needs lastTarget "card-contract" (here "code"); `undecided`/`continue`/`unreviewed` need verdict "unverified"/"pass"/"NONE". Stage `signal` is done (signal.pass "yes") and the read-only guard does not fire, so the skill sits in stage `review` and terminates on the unmatched-row path `BLOCK:review-unclassified`. The honest answer to "which row and effects apply" is therefore: none apply — and that is the defect (finding 1), because the ordinary code-repair path is unreachable at every ordinal.

The broken-record boundary wins. Row `broken-record` (line 39) matches — lastVerdict "finding", lastTarget "code", ordinal 3 >= 3, disposition "NONE" — and its effect list is [ASK]: the stage stops and asks rather than dispatching a fourth repair round, which is the declared meaning of `cycle: {counter: "review.ordinal", boundedBy: "broken-record"}` on the review stage — the counter bound takes precedence over the ordinary repair path. Two caveats matter for maintenance. (a) In the shipped artifact the boundary wins vacuously rather than by precedence: the inverted `open` predicate cannot match a finding at any ordinal, so the boundary is never actually contested and its precedence is untested. (b) Once `open` is repaired to `lastVerdict === "finding" && lastTarget === "code"`, it becomes a strict superset of `broken-record` while sitting ahead of it at rows[0]; the bound then only wins if the runtime honors `cycle.boundedBy` over row order — otherwise `broken-record` is shadowed and the review loop never terminates. Related: the disposition escape is currently broken the same way — {finding, code, ordinal 3, disposition "present"} matches neither `broken-record` (which demands disposition "NONE") nor `open`, so an explicitly dispositioned finding BLOCKs instead of resuming repair.

By blocking, under a named unclassified terminator. "mystery" is a legal member of the declared domain of review.lastVerdict (spec.mjs:6 — ["pass", "finding", "unverified", "mystery", "NONE"]) but no row in TABLES.review tests for it: `open` needs lastTarget "code" (here "NONE"), `broken-record`/`replan` need verdict "finding", `undecided` needs "unverified", `continue` needs "pass", `unreviewed` needs "NONE". TABLES.review declares `exclusive: false` and no default/fallback row, so the unmatched state resolves to the synthetic row `BLOCK:review-unclassified` with status BLOCK — exactly what the artifact's `unclassified` scenario expects. It does not silently fall through to a neighboring row and it does not advance: an in-domain value the table cannot classify terminates as an explicit block rather than a guess. Caveat worth flagging: this is the only BLOCK-on-unmatched path the fixtures exercise, and finding 1 pushes a state that SHOULD have been classified (verdict "finding", target "code", ordinal 1) onto this same terminator, so BLOCK:review-unclassified currently conflates "genuinely unclassifiable" with "row predicate is broken".

No. Guard `read-only-session` (spec.mjs:22) reads session.readOnly, which is "yes", so it fires with `then: "RESTRICT"` and `forbids: ["WRITE", "DISPATCH"]`. The skill must instead present the guard body (body.md "## guard: read-only-session"): explain that this session can inspect but cannot present a state-changing plan. Concretely in this state, signal.pass is "yes" so stage `signal` is done and stage `review` is active; with lastVerdict "NONE" the matching row is `unreviewed` (line 43), whose declared effects are [DISPATCH{role: reviewer}, WRITE{artifact: reviewLog, format: reviewResult}, NEXT]. Both DISPATCH and WRITE are forbidden, so the entire state-changing part of that row is withheld and only the restriction explanation is presented — the guard restricts effects, it does not rewrite or re-select the row. Note this path is completely unexercised: no scenario in fixtures/scenarios.json sets session.readOnly = "yes" (finding 5).

Root-cause concentration: findings 1 and 2 are one edit — the `!==` at spec.mjs:38. Restoring it to `s.review.lastVerdict === "finding" && s.review.lastTarget === "code"` re-enables the repair path and dissolves the overlap with `undecided` and `continue`, but it then makes rows[0] a strict superset of `broken-record` at rows[1]. Whoever applies that fix must confirm the runtime resolves `cycle.boundedBy` ahead of row order (or reorder the rows, or add an `ordinal < 3` clause), otherwise the cycle bound is shadowed and the review loop cannot terminate. See q3.

Checked and found consistent — reported as non-findings: all seven OBSERVATIONS have matching entries in collectors/index.mjs; every `body` reference in spec.mjs (why: purpose, guard: read-only-session, stage: signal/review/route, role: reviewer) has a corresponding section in body.md, and READ_FIRST's path resolves; TEMPLATES.report's fields {{status}} and {{evidence}} plus the required section "## Evidence" all appear in templates/review-report.md; OWNERSHIP paths match ARTIFACTS paths and writers; ROLES.reviewer declares `effects: []` (no state authority) and its judgment domain matches FORMATS.reviewResult's verdict domain; three stages sit well under the declared maxStages budget of 12; fixtures/lint/manifest.json covers L0-L18 with no gaps or duplicates. `route`'s `done: () => false` is deliberately not reported — it reads as an intentional terminal stage that always emits REPORT then DONE.

Uncertainty stated plainly: I cannot tell from inside the artifact whether the L0 import path is a planted defect or a consequence of copying the skill out of a tree where ./scripts/skill-rails/dsl.mjs resolved. Its status as a deliberate mutation is uncertain; its effect on the shipped artifact is not.
